pairs.difference: A (witch hat): the cone turns from light to dark in one long, soft front-lit gradient. There is no clear core shadow, the brim underside barely darkens, and form contrast is low (0.347). B (graduation cap): the top board is clearly lit with a crisp front corner, the skull band under it is in deep shade, and there is a distinct shadow under the board edge. That matches the side-and-top key on the real cards.
pairs.fix: Light the hat from the upper left. Keep the left side of the cone bright and put a clear darker band down the right side of the cone. Make the underside of the brim dark, and drop a soft shadow from the brim onto the band.

pairs.difference: A (candlestick): the lit flame lights nothing. The candle, the dish and the counter are all lit by a cool light from the left, and the gold base has a broad front sheen. B (vending machine): the left side is darker than the front, there is purple bounce on the floor, and the feet have contact shadows. It reads like the real cards.
pairs.fix: Let the flame cast a small warm glow on the top of the candle and the inside of the dish. Keep one main light from the upper left, with the right side of the stem in clear shadow.

pairs.difference: Both cards are below the real shading range. A (potion): the purple liquid glows from inside, so the round flask has no lit side or dark side, just an even inner glow. There is purple bounce on the table and a long cast shadow to the left. B (beach ball): the right side is lit, the left side turns into a clear shadow, and it sits in a dark contact shadow on the sand, so there is real form turn.
pairs.fix: Draw the flask as glass lit from the upper right: a bright highlight on the right shoulder, and the left side of the bulb darker. The liquid should glow only faintly, with a tight dark contact shadow where the flask meets the table.

pairs.difference: A (cauldron): the black belly is a broad, smooth gray-to-dark gradient with only faint highlights. It is lit almost from the front, and the soft cast shadow on the grass to the right does not match how the pot itself is shaded. B (lawnmower): the top of the red body has crisp highlights, the wheels are dark inside, and there is a contact shadow under the deck.
pairs.fix: Light the cauldron from the upper left. Put a bright curved highlight on the left of the belly and the rim, a deep shadow on the right side, and dark contact shadows under each leg.

pairs.difference: A (dead tree): the trunk and roots are lit evenly from the front, with no side of the trunk in shadow and no cast shadow on the grass. Form contrast (0.281) and light bias (0.092) are both below the real cards. B (topiary): each layer is lit on the left and dark underneath, and there is a strong shadow cast to the right across the lawn, like the real cards.
pairs.fix: Light the tree from the upper left. Make the right side of the trunk and the undersides of the branches clearly darker, put shadow inside the hollow, and cast a soft tree shadow across the grass to the right.

pairs.difference: A (lion statue): soft top-left light, with darker steps on the plinth to the right and a shadow cast onto the grass. Form contrast is low, but the light reads in one direction. B (water bottle): pale and lit evenly from the front, the bottle body has almost no dark side, and its shading range (0.459) is well below the real cards.
pairs.fix: Give the bottle a clear light side and dark side. Light it from the upper left with a soft white sheen down the left edge, and let the right side of the body fall into a deeper blue shadow.

pairs.difference: A (scout jacket): the key light comes from the upper left, the right sleeve and the folds are clearly in shadow, and the cuffs are dark inside. B (jack-o-lantern): the pumpkin is lit straight from the front, and the ribs read as even bands with no dark side. The glowing face does not light the pumpkin around it. Form contrast is 0.413.
pairs.fix: Light the pumpkin from the upper left. Put a broad sheen on the left ribs and let the right half turn into deep orange-brown shadow. Add a warm glow on the cut edges of the eyes and mouth.

pairs.difference: A (coaster cars): soft top light, with lit seat backs and darker undersides. B (diploma): a hard spotlight from one side with a glossy mirror reflection on the blue table. Light bias is 0.924, well above the real cards (0.191 to 0.641).
pairs.fix: Use a softer, broader light on the scroll. Let the far end shade only gently, and replace the mirror reflection on the table with a soft contact shadow under the roll.

pairs.difference: A (pool sheep): soft top light, with gentle shade under the arms and the hat. B (ghost sheep): dusk rim light along the sheet, with deep, sharp dark creases in the sheet folds. The glowing pumpkin does not light the sheep's legs beside it, and the sheet's shadow is deeper than the soft shadows on the real cards.
pairs.fix: Use soft daylight from the upper left. Shade the sheet folds gently, without black creases, and let the pumpkin cast a small warm glow on the nearby leg and the grass.

pairs.difference: A (jellyfish): a translucent bell with inner glow and rays of light from above. Its shading range is low, but that comes from transparency. B (bat): lit from the front and symmetrical. Both wings and the face are equally bright, and there is no dark side on the body. The backlit sunburst puts no rim light on the wing edges.
pairs.fix: Light the bat from the upper left. Make the left wing brighter and put the right wing and the right side of the body in darker shadow. Add a thin warm rim along the wing edges from the bright background.

pairs.difference: A (fruit plate): directional top light, with a lit watermelon face, shaded edges on the fruit and a rim highlight on the glass plate. B (candy corn): a broad, flat front light, and the cone barely turns from left to right. Shading range is 0.522 and form contrast 0.317, both below the real cards. The strong cast shadow on the left is the only sign of a light direction.
pairs.fix: Light the candy corn from the upper right. Put a soft sheen on the right of the tip and let the left side of the cone turn clearly darker, matching the cast shadow on the left.

pairs.difference: A (house): the walls and the tower are lit almost from the front, with both faces at similar brightness. The window glow does not light the walls, and the ground lens shows a dark patch on the right that does not match any light on the house. B (gate): the sun comes from the left, so the left faces of the pillars are bright, the right faces are shaded, and the shadows on the paving match.
pairs.fix: Light the house from the upper left. Keep the front wall bright, put the side wall and the right of the tower in clear shadow, and cast a soft house shadow to the right on the grass. Let the windows throw a faint warm glow on the sills.

pattern: Generated cards are lit from the front and too evenly. Light turns into shadow as one long soft gradient with no clear core shadow, so one side of the hero never falls into shadow the way it does on the real cards. Glowing parts (flame, jack-o-lantern face, potion, windows) glow but do not light the surfaces next to them. The cast shadow often shows a light direction that the object's own shading does not follow.
